headline: Revenue up 161% to $14.6B, first profit as a listed company
summary: SpaceX revenue rose 161% to $14.6B and net income was $4.4B, against a $1.1B loss a year earlier, as AI revenue reached $7.6B. Up to 1.3 billion locked-up shares become free to sell at the start of Thursday 22 October 2026, two trading days after these results.
points: AI became the largest segment: revenue rose 830% to $7.56B on new cloud services agreements, the Cursor acquisition (completed 14 August, adding $608M of revenue) and wider Grok adoption.
Starlink consumer subscribers rose by 1.6 million in the quarter to 13.6 million, and monthly ARPU rose 5% from Q2 to $69, though it was $83 a year earlier.
Starship Flight 14, its first orbital flight and first revenue-generating mission, delivered 26 Starlink V3 satellites, about 10 times the downlink capacity added by a Falcon 9 Starlink launch.
Of the $19.6B capital spending, $16.4B went to the AI segment as the COLOSSUS II compute buildout continued; SpaceX also agreed on 8 October to buy 800 MHz spectrum licences for Starlink Mobile.
On the results call, according to Reuters and CNBC, SpaceX said Tesla and SpaceX had formed special board committees to discuss a possible merger.
guidance: The results release gave no numerical outlook. On the call SpaceX guided to Q1 2027 revenue of $33B to $37B, against an analyst average of $22.2B (LSEG, via CNBC), and Q4 2026 capital spending of $35B to $40B, according to Reuters. The finance chief reiterated a target of about $100B of annual recurring revenue by the end of 2026, and management expects Q4 gross margins to normalise after one-time benefits in Q3 and nameplate compute of 2.5 to 3 GW by the end of the year, according to Investing.com.
reaction: SPCX closed the regular session at $147.79 on 20 October, according to Investing.com. Shares were up 4.9% in extended trading after the call, according to Reuters at 18:25 ET (23:25 UK time); CNBC reported a gain of about 5% and Investing.com a later after-hours price of $157.59, up 6.6%. Revenue of $14.58B beat the $12.72B analyst average and adjusted EPS of 45 cents beat 13 cents (LSEG, via CNBC). Reuters attributed the rise to comments on the call about a possible merger with Tesla.
sources: SpaceX Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results (SpaceX investor relations)
SpaceX quarterly revenue jumps, beats estimates as AI business surges (Reuters)

analysis: AI is now SpaceX's biggest business

For the first time the Super Intelligence segment brought in more revenue than Starlink: $7.56B against $5.25B, or 52% of the group total. Almost all of that growth came from SI solutions and infrastructure, which rose from $359M a year earlier and $2.19B in Q2 to $7.02B, mostly from renting data-centre capacity to other AI developers, according to Reuters. Cursor added $608M. Advertising revenue grew 18% to $538M.

On the call, according to transcripts published by Investing.com and Benzinga, the finance chief said compute pricing was tracking slightly above the top of the $30 to $50 per watt range given last quarter, and that new deployments were paying back in less than a year at current prices. Those are management claims and cannot be checked from the accounts yet.
Starlink is still where the reliable profit is

Connectivity earned $2.37B of operating income at a 45.1% margin, up from 38.4% a year earlier, and spent only $1.54B on capital projects. The AI segment made $431M at a 5.7% margin while spending $16.44B. That gap is the main tension in the story: the business that is growing fastest is also the one consuming nearly all the cash.

Starlink grew revenue by volume rather than price. Consumer subscribers rose 89% in a year to 13.6 million while consumer ARPU fell 17% to $69, so consumer revenue rose 57%. Enterprise and government revenue grew faster, up 91% to $2.13B, and Connectivity selling and administrative costs roughly tripled to $325M as marketing increased.
The headline profit flatters the underlying result

Net income of $4.40B was well above operating income of $2.79B. About $1.61B came from below the operating line: other income of $1.03B (of which $561M was from related parties), net interest income of $198M and a tax benefit of $390M. Over the first nine months of 2026 SpaceX still made a net loss of $413M.

Management also said, according to Investing.com, that Q4 gross margins should normalise after one-time benefits in Q3. Against that, operating income was held back by $1.22B of share-based pay from the Cursor deal. SpaceX says $23.4B of Cursor-related equity awards is attributable to future service, so that charge will recur for some time.
The cash bill is getting bigger, not smaller

In the first nine months SpaceX generated $13.10B of operating cash flow and spent $48.07B on property and equipment, a gap of about $35B covered mostly by $85.7B of net IPO proceeds and about $12.0B of net new borrowing. It ended September with $89.9B of cash and marketable securities against $38.8B of debt and finance leases, up from $22.9B at the end of 2025.

Guidance points to spending accelerating: $35B to $40B of capital spending in Q4 alone, which would take the 2026 total to roughly $83B to $88B. The cash pile can carry that for now, but the return on this spending is the question the next few quarters have to answer.
Guidance and backlog are the reason the shares rose

Q1 2027 revenue guidance of $33B to $37B is 2.3 to 2.5 times Q3 revenue and well above the $22.2B analyst average reported by CNBC. SpaceX reported a $63B backlog at 30 September, with about $42B expected to be recognised within 12 months, according to the call transcripts, and $17.5B already received as deferred revenue on the balance sheet. That backlog gives the near-term forecast some contracted support.

The space segment was the weak spot. Revenue rose 6% to $1.77B even though launches fell to 35 from 44 a year earlier, but research and development rose 44% to $1.23B as Starship spending increased, leaving a $7M operating loss.
What analysts said

"SpaceX delivered the quarter the bulls wanted, at least on the top line. The story now is all about AI," Will Rhind, chief executive of GraniteShares, told Reuters. Daniel Newman, chief executive of the Futurum Group, told Reuters that AI revenue was "quickly providing operating strength and leverage" for the satellite and launch businesses.

Investing.com listed the main risks raised around the results as heavy capital spending, execution risk from building Starship, satellites and compute at the same time, regulatory approvals and margins that may not repeat.
analysisNote: Analysis by Orbit Alpha from the SpaceX results release and the sources below. Percentages and totals not stated by SpaceX are Orbit Alpha calculations from reported figures.
watch: Thursday 22 October 2026: up to 1.3 billion locked-up shares become free to sell at the start of trading. Before the first release of more than 911 million shares on 6 August, the stock hit a low of $104.83 on 3 August and then rallied once the shares were released, according to CNBC. Dates are on the SpaceX lockup calendar.
Q4 capital spending against the $35B to $40B guidance, and whether nameplate compute reaches the 2.5 to 3 GW management targeted by the end of the year (1.7 GW at 30 September).
Whether gross margins fall back in Q4, as management indicated after one-time benefits in Q3.
Starlink kit deliveries and activations in Q4. Management said it prioritised retail stock ahead of the holiday season, according to the Investing.com transcript.
Progress of the Tesla merger talks, which would need shareholder approval on both sides, according to Reuters and CNBC.
SpaceX has not yet announced its Q4 2026 results date.
faq: Did SpaceX make a profit in Q3 2026?

Yes. SpaceX reported net income of $4.40B for the three months to 30 September 2026, against a net loss of $1.05B a year earlier, and income from operations of $2.79B. About $1.61B of the net income came from other income, net interest income and a tax benefit rather than operations.
How much revenue did Starlink make in Q3 2026?
SpaceX's Connectivity segment, which is mainly Starlink, had revenue of $5.25B, up 69%: $3.12B from consumers and $2.13B from enterprise and government customers.
How many Starlink subscribers are there?

13.6 million Starlink consumer subscribers at 30 September 2026, up from 12.0 million at the end of June and 7.2 million a year earlier, plus hundreds of thousands of enterprise subscribers, according to SpaceX.
What is SpaceX's guidance?

The results release gave no numerical outlook. On the call SpaceX guided to Q1 2027 revenue of $33B to $37B and Q4 2026 capital spending of $35B to $40B, and said it expects about $100B of annual recurring revenue by the end of 2026, according to Reuters, CNBC and Investing.com.
When do more SpaceX shares unlock?
Up to 1.3 billion locked-up shares become free to sell at the start of Thursday 22 October 2026, two trading days after the Q3 results. The full schedule is on the SpaceX lockup calendar.

headline: Revenue down 20% to C$81M, net loss widens to C$157M
summary: Telesat revenue fell 20% to C$81M and adjusted EBITDA fell 74% to C$12M, including C$25M of debt refinancing costs, while the net loss widened to C$157M. LEO backlog stood at about C$5.6B after a C$2.7B Canadian military Lightspeed deal.
points: Signed a C$2.7B agreement, including options, with Canada's Defence Investment Agency to supply Lightspeed military Ka-band services under the ESCP-P programme, with C$2.0B of milestone payments expected between Q3 2026 and Q4 2028.
The initial Lightspeed constellation has grown to a planned 225 satellites from 156, with high latitude commercial service expected around the end of Q1 2028.
Excluding C$25M of debt refinancing costs, GEO adjusted EBITDA fell 23% and the GEO margin was 78%, against 79% a year earlier.
Customer prepayments of C$510M in the first nine months lifted operating cash flow to C$405M, from C$97M.
The company said it remains focused on refinancing the Telesat GEO debt, which begins to mature later this year.
guidance: Telesat reiterated 2026 GEO revenue of C$300M to C$320M and GEO adjusted EBITDA of C$210M to C$230M, excluding refinancing costs. It lowered expected 2026 Lightspeed spending to C$1.1B to C$1.3B, from C$1.3B to C$1.5B, to reflect the timing of satellite and launch payments.
reaction: Shares were down 1.9% at $44.69 on Nasdaq at 10:26 a.m. New York time (14:26 UK) on 29 October, against a previous close of $45.55.
sources: Telesat: results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 (GlobeNewswire)
Telesat: Q3 Earnings Snapshot (Associated Press via Yahoo Finance)
faq: Why did Telesat's revenue fall in Q3 2026?

Revenue fell 20% to C$80.6M because the GEO satellite business, which brings in almost all of Telesat's revenue today, fell 21% to C$79M. Adjusted EBITDA also included C$25M of debt refinancing costs; without them GEO adjusted EBITDA fell 23% and the GEO margin was 78%, against 79% a year earlier.
How big is Telesat's Lightspeed backlog?

About C$5.6B at 30 September 2026, after a C$2.7B agreement, including options, with Canada's Defence Investment Agency for Lightspeed military Ka-band services. The planned initial constellation has grown to 225 satellites from 156, with high latitude commercial service expected around the end of the first quarter of 2028.
How much cash does Telesat have?

C$813.8M at 30 September 2026, up from C$509.8M at the end of 2025, helped by C$510M of customer prepayments in the first nine months. It invested C$368M in Lightspeed in the quarter and lowered expected 2026 Lightspeed spending to C$1.1B to C$1.3B, from C$1.3B to C$1.5B.

headline: Revenue up 124% to $89M, backlog at a record $742M
summary: Voyager revenue rose 124% to $88.7M and bookings rose 135% to $116M, while the net loss widened to $55.7M from $16.3M. Backlog reached a record $742M, including $347M from the Astrobotic acquisition, and the low end of 2026 revenue guidance was raised by $10M.
metrics: +293% year on year; from $336M at 30 June
points: Backlog more than doubled from the second quarter, helped by $347M added through the Astrobotic acquisition, including a $298M NASA award.
Starlab commercial reservations rose to about $700M from about $500M last quarter; cumulative milestone cash receipts reached $212.5M.
NASA released its Commercial LEO Destination Phase 2 request for proposals in October, with submissions due in December 2026 and an award expected in spring 2027.
Announced a strategic partnership with Anduril and completed Griffin-1 acceptance testing ahead of a planned late 2026 launch.
Convertible notes stood at $841.1M, net, at the end of the quarter.
guidance: Voyager raised the lower end of its 2026 revenue guidance by $10M, to a range of $285M to $305M, which it said represents growth of about 72% to 84%.
sources: Voyager Reports Record Third Quarter 2026 Revenue, Bookings and Backlog (Business Wire via Morningstar)
Voyager Technologies Q3 revenue beats; low end of 2026 outlook range raised (Reuters via TradingView)
Voyager Technologies Reports Mixed Q3, Revenue Up 124% Year-Over-Year (Benzinga)
faq: Why did Voyager's backlog more than double?

Backlog reached a record $742M at 30 September 2026, from $336M at 30 June. The Astrobotic acquisition added $347M, including a $298M NASA award, and bookings in the quarter were $116M, a book-to-bill of 1.3x.
What is Voyager's 2026 revenue guidance?
$285M to $305M, after Voyager raised the low end by $10M. The company says that range is growth of about 72% to 84%.
When will NASA choose its commercial space stations?

NASA released its Commercial LEO Destination Phase 2 request for proposals in October 2026, with submissions due in December 2026 and an award expected in spring 2027. Voyager's Starlab station had about $700M of commercial reservations at the end of the quarter.

headline: Revenue up 5.4% to $109M, record backlog of $619.7M
summary: Redwire revenue rose 5.4% to $109.0M and gross margin reached a record 32.3%, up from 16.3%, while the net loss narrowed to $23.2M from $41.2M. Backlog hit a record $619.7M, book-to-bill was 1.73 and 2026 revenue guidance of $450M to $500M was reaffirmed.
metrics: record; up nearly 75% year on year
points: Space revenue grew to $61.3M while Defense Tech revenue fell to $47.8M from $56.9M a year earlier.
Research and development spending rose 87.1% to $14.4M, which the company cited as the main reason adjusted EBITDA slipped.
Won a $20M DARPA contract for further testing of a scaled SabreSat spacecraft ahead of a very low Earth orbit flight test.
Received a follow-on Axiom Space order for two Roll-Out Solar Array wings, and after the quarter launched the final pair of ISS solar arrays.
Secured follow-on Stalker drone orders, including from the US National Guard.
guidance: Redwire reaffirmed its forecast of $450M to $500M in revenue for 2026, having recorded $323.1M in the first nine months.
reaction: Shares were down 8.23% at $7.08 in after-hours trading on 4 November, per Benzinga at about 4:45pm ET.
sources: Redwire Corporation Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results, Expands Backlog, Achieves Record Gross Margins (Business Wire)
Redwire Stock Slips as Uneven Revenue Timing Softens Q3 Results (Benzinga)
faq: How did Redwire shares react to Q3 2026 results?

They were down 8.23% at $7.08 in after-hours trading on 4 November. Revenue grew 5.4% to $109.0M as Space revenue rose to $61.3M while Defense Tech revenue fell to $47.8M from $56.9M, and adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $5.3M, against a loss of $2.6M, as research and development spending rose 87.1%.
What does Redwire need in Q4 to hit its 2026 guidance?

Redwire reaffirmed 2026 revenue of $450M to $500M after recording $323.1M in the first nine months. That leaves $126.9M to $176.9M for the fourth quarter (our calculation), against $109.0M in the third quarter.
How big is Redwire's backlog?
A record $619.7M, up nearly 75% from a year earlier. Contracts awarded in the quarter were $188.7M, a book-to-bill of 1.73. Redwire also won a $20M DARPA contract for further SabreSat testing.

headline: Record revenue up 118% to $42.8M, net income of $18.5M
summary: BlackSky revenue rose 118% to a record $42.8M and it swung to net income of $18.5M from a $15.3M loss, with record adjusted EBITDA of $12.8M. It raised 2026 guidance to revenue of $140M to $150M and adjusted EBITDA of $18M to $24M.
metrics: Cash, restricted cash and short-term investments
points: Net income was helped by a $19.7M gain on derivatives; operating income was $0.4M.
Deployed a fifth Gen-3 satellite, which reached first light and revenue-generating operations within 24 hours.
Named exclusive provider of very high resolution optical satellites for a $1B consortium investment including France and the UAE, covering an initial 50-satellite constellation.
An international defence customer moved from a small Gen-2 pilot to a seven-figure Gen-3 Assured subscription in under six months.
Won a seven-figure renewal with HEO for non-Earth imaging space domain awareness services.
guidance: BlackSky raised its 2026 outlook for the second time this year, to revenue of $140M to $150M and adjusted EBITDA of $18M to $24M, and kept capital expenditure guidance at $50M to $60M.
sources: BlackSky Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results, Exhibit 99.1 (SEC EDGAR)
BlackSky Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results (Business Wire via Yahoo Finance)
BlackSky Reports $42.8 Million Revenue and $18.5 Million Net Income (TradingView)

analysis: The growth is in the highest-margin line

Space-based intelligence and AI services, BlackSky's imagery and analytics subscriptions, more than doubled to $32.7M and made up 76.4% of revenue. Its direct costs were $4.9M, so before depreciation that line kept about 85 cents of every dollar. Across the whole business, direct costs fell to 21.2% of revenue from 34.7% a year earlier.

Overheads grew far more slowly than sales. Selling, general and administrative costs rose 16.8% to $25.4M while revenue rose 118%, which is why the operating line moved from a $16.8M loss to a $0.4M profit.
The profit is mostly an accounting gain

Net income of $18.5M included a $19.7M gain on derivatives. Without it, pre-tax income would have been a loss of about $1.2M. The derivative gain also explains the gap between basic earnings per share of $0.45 and diluted earnings per share of $0.10.

The more durable improvement is in cash. Operating cash outflow for the first nine months was $2.3M, against $19.0M a year earlier, so the core business is now close to funding itself before capital spending.
Guidance implies Q3 is a new floor

Nine-month revenue was $96.9M, up 35.8%. The raised full-year range of $140M to $150M therefore implies Q4 revenue of roughly $43M to $53M, at or above the record Q3 level. This was the second guidance increase of the year.
Adjusted EBITDA guidance rose to $18M to $24M and capital spending guidance stayed at $50M to $60M. In the first nine months BlackSky spent $46.5M on property, equipment and satellites in progress.
International customers are carrying more of the story

The headline commercial win was selection as exclusive provider of very high resolution optical satellites for a $1B consortium investment including France and the UAE, covering an initial 50-satellite constellation. An international defence customer also moved from a small Gen-2 pilot to a seven-figure Gen-3 Assured subscription in under six months.

That pattern, a pilot followed by a larger subscription, is how BlackSky is trying to turn one-off contracts into recurring revenue. A wider international base also reduces dependence on US government budgets, though the US government remains a customer through pilots such as the seven-figure assured Gen-3 trial completed in the quarter.
The cost of getting here

BlackSky raised $160.0M of equity, net of costs, in the first nine months of 2026, and the basic weighted average share count rose 15.7% from a year earlier to 40.7M. It ended September with $231.1M of cash, restricted cash and short-term investments.

watch: Q4 revenue against the $43M to $53M implied by full-year guidance.
Further Gen-3 satellite launches and how quickly each reaches revenue-generating operations.
Progress on the France and UAE consortium programme, the largest commercial opportunity named in the release.
Whether net income continues to swing with derivative gains and losses, which can move the headline result in either direction.
faq: Did BlackSky make a profit in Q3 2026?
BlackSky reported net income of $18.5M for the three months to 30 September 2026, against a $15.3M loss a year earlier. That included a $19.7M gain on derivatives; operating income was $0.4M.
What is BlackSky's 2026 revenue guidance?
BlackSky raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $140M to $150M and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $18M to $24M, and kept capital spending guidance at $50M to $60M.
How much cash does BlackSky have?
BlackSky had $231.1M of cash, restricted cash and short-term investments at 30 September 2026.

headline: Revenue up 21.5% to C$498.1M, 2026 guidance raised
summary: MDA Space revenue rose 21.5% to C$498.1M and net income reached C$30.9M, up from C$27.0M, while adjusted EBITDA grew 15.9% to C$96.0M. It raised 2026 revenue guidance to C$1.90B to C$1.95B; backlog stood at C$3.95B.
metrics: from C$4,392.8M; in line with Q2
from net debt of C$120.0M at end of 2025
points: Satellite Systems growth was driven mainly by the Telesat Lightspeed programme; Robotics revenue came from steady Canadarm3 work.
Selected to take part in Europe's IRIS2 satellite programme.
Deployed the first satellites it built for Globalstar's existing constellation and began operations at a new high-volume satellite factory.
Launched two defence-focused products, MDA MIDNIGHT and MDA AURORA BLACK, and issued C$600M of senior unsecured notes in August.
Total liquidity of C$2.9B is earmarked partly for the pending acquisitions of CLS and Blue Canyon Technologies.
guidance: MDA raised 2026 guidance to revenue of C$1.90B to C$1.95B (from C$1.8B to C$1.9B) and adjusted EBITDA of C$355M to C$375M (from C$330M to C$370M), and reaffirmed an 18% to 20% adjusted EBITDA margin.
sources: MDA Space Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results (PR Newswire)
MDA Space reports $30.9M Q3 profit, raises guidance for full year (CTV News)
MDA Space to acquire Blue Canyon Technologies, Form 6-K, June 2026 (SEC EDGAR)
analysis: One programme is driving the growth

Satellite Systems, where the Telesat Lightspeed constellation is the main contract, grew by about C$75M and accounted for 71.9% of revenue. Robotics, built around Canadarm3, grew 2.0%, and Geointelligence grew 24.8% on new programmes.

That mix explains the slight margin squeeze. Large satellite manufacturing work carries lower margins than MDA's other lines, and gross margin slipped to 25.3% from 26.4% while adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 19.3% from 20.2%, still inside the 18% to 20% full-year range.
Guidance points to a quieter Q4

MDA booked C$1,460.8M of revenue in the first nine months, up 28.8%. The new full-year range therefore implies Q4 revenue of about C$439M to C$489M and Q4 adjusted EBITDA of about C$72M to C$92M, both below Q3's C$498.1M and C$96.0M. Raising the annual number while implying a softer final quarter indicates management does not expect Q3's pace to repeat in Q4.
Backlog is being consumed faster than it is replaced
Bookings rose to C$444.2M from C$174.2M, but that was still less than revenue, a book-to-bill ratio of 0.89. Backlog of C$3,949.1M was 10.1% lower than a year earlier, though level with Q2.

For a company whose revenue rests on a few very large programmes, the size of the next big award matters more than any single quarter. MDA cites a C$40B opportunity pipeline, and its selection for Europe's IRIS2 programme is one route to refilling the backlog.
Turning cash into a broader business

MDA ended the quarter with C$1,328.0M of net cash, against C$120.0M of net debt at the end of 2025, and C$2.9B of total liquidity after issuing C$600M of senior unsecured notes in August. Free cash flow was C$61.6M in the quarter.

That cash is earmarked for the pending acquisitions of CLS and Blue Canyon Technologies. Blue Canyon, bought from RTX's Raytheon business for US$620M in cash, makes small satellites and components in Colorado and gives MDA a manufacturing base in the US defence market; MDA said it adds US$3.5B to its opportunity pipeline and expects it to add to adjusted EBITDA and adjusted earnings per share in 2027.

Alongside its own CHORUS Earth observation constellation, due to launch later in 2026, and the MDA MIDNIGHT and MDA AURORA BLACK defence products, the deals move MDA from a contract manufacturer towards a company that also owns satellites, sells data and competes for US defence work.
Profit per share is not keeping up
Adjusted net income rose 26.1% to C$60.4M, but adjusted diluted earnings per share was flat at C$0.37 because of a higher average share count. Net income rose 14.4% to C$30.9M.
analysisNote: Analysis by Orbit Alpha from the MDA Space results release and the sources below. Percentages, implied figures and totals not stated by MDA Space are Orbit Alpha calculations from reported figures.
watch: Completion of the Blue Canyon Technologies acquisition, expected by the end of 2026, and the CLS deal.
Launch of the CHORUS constellation, scheduled for later in 2026.
Q4 bookings and backlog, after a book-to-bill of 0.89 in Q3.
Q4 revenue against the C$439M to C$489M implied by full-year guidance.
Contract awards under Europe's IRIS2 programme.
faq: Did MDA Space raise its guidance?
Yes. MDA raised 2026 revenue guidance to C$1.90B to C$1.95B from C$1.8B to C$1.9B, and adjusted EBITDA guidance to C$355M to C$375M from C$330M to C$370M.
What is MDA Space's backlog?
MDA's backlog was C$3,949.1M at 30 September 2026, down from C$4,392.8M a year earlier and in line with Q2 2026.
Are MDA Space's figures in Canadian dollars?
Yes. MDA reports in Canadian dollars, and all figures on this page are in C$ unless stated.

headline: Revenue down 4% to $70.9M, net loss of $15.7M
summary: Globalstar revenue fell to $70.9M from $73.8M and it posted a net loss of $15.7M against net income of $1.1M a year earlier, as non-cash imputed interest rose. Adjusted EBITDA was $30.3M, down from $37.6M.
points: Service revenue fell mainly on lower wholesale capacity revenue, timing of network cost reimbursements and churn in Duplex and SPOT, partly offset by Commercial IoT.
Commercial IoT reached record activations on a last twelve months basis, with gross activations up 25%.
Launched the first set of HIBLEO-4 replacement satellites during the quarter.
Received a key FCC authorisation and a German regulatory authorisation for the C-3 constellation, and expanded its ground station in Greece.
The FCC Space Bureau approved Amazon's application to acquire Globalstar's FCC licences in October; the deal is expected to close in 2027.
guidance: Globalstar gave no guidance and, with the Amazon transaction pending, said it does not intend to hold future earnings calls.
sources: Globalstar Announces Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results, Exhibit 99.1 (SEC EDGAR)
Globalstar Announces Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results (GlobeNewswire)
GSAT: Q3 losses widened as network investment continued and the Amazon merger advanced (TradingView)
Globalstar Form 8-K, Amazon merger announcement, April 2026 (SEC EDGAR)
analysis: The quarter matters less than the deal

Amazon agreed in April 2026 to acquire Globalstar for $90.00 per share in cash, or 0.3210 Amazon shares with the value capped at $90.00, with cash elections limited to 40% of shares. The price can be cut by up to $110M if Globalstar misses certain operational milestones, and closing depends on HIBLEO-4 replacement satellite milestones. The deal is expected to close in 2027.

Globalstar gave no guidance this quarter and said it does not intend to hold future earnings calls. For shareholders, progress on the satellites and approvals now carries more weight than quarterly revenue.
Progress on the conditions that count

The first set of HIBLEO-4 replacement satellites launched in Q3, the first step towards the milestones the deal depends on. In October the FCC Space Bureau approved Amazon's application to acquire Globalstar's FCC licences.
Work on the next-generation C-3 system also moved forward, with a key FCC authorisation, a German regulatory authorisation and completed ground station construction in the US, Canada and Greece.
Why profit fell

Service revenue fell 6.1% to $65.4M, mainly from lower wholesale capacity revenue, the timing of network cost reimbursements and churn in Duplex and SPOT. Adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 42.7% from 50.9%.

The net loss of $15.7M was driven mainly by higher non-cash imputed interest linked to the 2024 Prepayment Agreement, so it overstates the decline in the underlying business. Income from operations was still positive at $7.6M.
The subscriber base is changing shape

Commercial IoT grew 8.9% to 591,114 average subscribers, with record activations on a last twelve months basis, and its ARPU rose to $4.34. The higher-value consumer products are shrinking: Duplex subscribers fell 27.4% and SPOT 8.0%. Duplex earns more than 17 times as much per user each month as IoT, so the growth in subscriber numbers does not translate into revenue growth.
Subscriber equipment sales rose 31% to $5.5M, a sign of continuing IoT device demand.
Cash is going into the network

Cash fell to $329.9M at 30 September from $447.5M at the end of 2025, while debt principal edged up to $414.7M. Adjusted free cash flow for the first nine months roughly halved to $66.8M from $133.3M, reflecting spending on HIBLEO-4, C-3 and ground infrastructure.
analysisNote: Analysis by Orbit Alpha from the Globalstar results release and the sources below. Percentages, implied figures and totals not stated by Globalstar are Orbit Alpha calculations from reported figures. Deal terms are from the merger announcement filed with the SEC in April 2026.
watch: Further HIBLEO-4 launches and whether Globalstar meets the satellite milestones the Amazon deal depends on.
Remaining regulatory approvals for the Amazon transaction, expected to close in 2027.
C-3 system progress following the FCC and German authorisations.
Globalstar will not hold further earnings calls, so filings and press releases are now the main source of updates.
faq: Is Amazon buying Globalstar?

Yes. Amazon agreed in April 2026 to acquire Globalstar for $90.00 per share in cash or 0.3210 Amazon shares capped at $90.00, subject to a downward adjustment of up to $110M if certain operational milestones are missed. Closing is expected in 2027.
Why did Globalstar report a loss in Q3 2026?
Globalstar's $15.7M net loss was mainly due to higher non-cash imputed interest linked to its 2024 Prepayment Agreement. It made $7.6M of income from operations.
Will Globalstar hold earnings calls?
No. Globalstar said that, given the pending Amazon transaction, it does not intend to hold future earnings conference calls.

points: Hypersonics and Strategic Missile Defense revenue rose 39.6% to $51.1M and Tactical Missiles and Integrated Defense Systems rose 51.9% to $67.6M.

Yes. Karman now expects fiscal 2026 revenue of $755M to $760M and adjusted EBITDA of $225M to $227M, excluding future acquisitions.

points: ViaSat-3 Flight 2 and Flight 3 both entered service, covering the Americas and Asia-Pacific.

faq: Which part of Viasat is growing?
Defense and Advanced Technologies, where revenue rose 20% to $365M and backlog reached a record $1.4B. Communication Services revenue fell 3% to $815M, so total revenue rose 3% to $1.18B.
What changed in Viasat's guidance?
Viasat still expects mid-single-digit revenue growth in fiscal 2027, but now sees adjusted EBITDA about flat. It expects capital expenditure of $850M to $900M and free cash flow of more than $225M.

headline: Revenue down 69% to $1.13B on deconsolidation, net income $2.78B
summary: EchoStar revenue fell to $1.13B from $3.61B after Pay-TV and Broadband were deconsolidated, while net income was $2.78B against a $12.78B loss, lifted by a $3.11B AT&T spectrum sale gain. Wireless lost 182,000 subscribers to 7.19M.
points: Revenue fell mainly because substantially all of the Pay-TV and Other segments were deconsolidated from 30 June 2026 and substantially all of Broadband and Satellite Services from 31 July 2026.
The AT&T spectrum sale closed on 28 July 2026, bringing $20.25B in cash, with a further $2.4B paid by AT&T directly into the Wireless Creditor Trust.
DISH DBS emerged from its prepackaged Chapter 11 on 1 October 2026 and will be reconsolidated; the DISH Wireless Chapter 11 cases remain pending.
The SpaceX spectrum licences were transferred to a trust in May 2026, with the acquisition closing still targeted for 30 November 2027.
EchoStar reported through its 10-Q only, with no results press release or conference call.
reaction: Shares were at $101.80, up more than 3%, in early morning trading on 3 November 2026, according to Fierce Network.

faq: Why did EchoStar's revenue fall 69%?

Mostly accounting: substantially all of the Pay-TV and Other segments were deconsolidated from 30 June 2026 and substantially all of Broadband and Satellite Services from 31 July 2026. Wireless revenue, now the bulk of what remains, fell 3.4% to $905.2M.
Why did EchoStar report a $2.78B profit?

Net income was lifted by a one-off $3.11B gain on the AT&T spectrum sale, which closed on 28 July 2026 and brought $20.25B in cash, with a further $2.4B paid by AT&T into the Wireless Creditor Trust. EchoStar ended the quarter with $13.44B of cash and equivalents.

The SpaceX spectrum licences were transferred to a trust in May 2026, and closing of the acquisition is still targeted for 30 November 2027.

Twelve Rocket Lab-built spacecraft launched and are operating, including eight Globalstar satellite platforms and twin NASA Mars science spacecraft, with more than 55 in development and build.
The pending Iridium acquisition is now fully funded and has Iridium shareholder approval.
guidance: For Q4 2026 Rocket Lab expects revenue of $270M to $290M, GAAP gross margin of 34% to 36%, non-GAAP gross margin of 39% to 41% and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $14M to $20M.

No earlier than 2027. The first Neutron flight hardware has been delivered to Launch Complex 3, and Neutron contracts worth over $515M signed in the quarter took its backlog to 16 missions.

Revenue of $270M to $290M, GAAP gross margin of 34% to 36%, non-GAAP gross margin of 39% to 41% and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $14M to $20M.

$4.45B at 30 September 2026, up from $828.7M at the end of 2025, and operating cash flow was positive at $7.2M in the quarter. The pending Iridium acquisition is fully funded and has Iridium shareholder approval.

$150M to $200M, which the company said it remains on target for, with possible upside from recent contracts. Third-quarter revenue was $42.3M, from gateway deliveries and US Government milestones.

headline: Record revenue up 342% to $16.0M, adjusted EBITDA positive
summary: Satellogic revenue rose 342% to a record $16.0M from $3.6M a year earlier, and adjusted EBITDA was positive at $1.2M. GAAP net income of $28.3M included a $30.0M non-cash fair value gain.
points: Merlin.01 launched on 1 October and is operating, with payload commissioning under way.
Two NewSat Mark VI satellites and a sovereign-programme NewSat Mark V also launched on 1 October.
After the quarter, agreed to transfer three in-orbit satellites for about $37M, not yet in the backlog figure.
Delivered the second CEiiA satellite under an $18M agreement with Portugal.
Signed a three-year non-Earth imaging agreement with HEO with a seven-figure minimum annual commitment.
guidance: Satellogic gave no numerical guidance; it plans further Merlin launches in the first half of 2027, with initial Merlin revenue expected in the second half of 2027.

faq: Is Satellogic profitable?

Adjusted EBITDA was positive at $1.2M, against negative $4.9M a year earlier, but the company still made an operating loss of $2.3M. GAAP net income of $28.3M included a $30.0M non-cash fair value gain.
Why did Satellogic's revenue rise 342%?
Space Systems revenue, from selling and building satellites, rose to $9.5M from $0.5M, and Data and Analytics revenue rose to $6.6M from $3.2M, for a record $16.0M in total.
When will Merlin start earning revenue?

Merlin.01 launched on 1 October 2026 and is operating, with payload commissioning under way. Satellogic plans further Merlin launches in the first half of 2027 and expects initial Merlin revenue in the second half of 2027.
